focusLock.decision: The iOS 3.0 App Store submission is the release goal. The Mac app and the CLI 3.0.0 are public since 2026-10-23, released from the signed v3.0.0 commit e7a8e2ae, which is the freeze commit. iPhone candidates are v<version>-ios.N tags cut by scripts/ios_candidate_tag.py on the maintainer's request; since the freeze the maintainer has added iPhone changes only as items of this plan (RF-35, RF-36, RF-37). A new finding joins this plan only if it risks App Review rejection, a crash or hang, data loss, a broken purchase or restore, or a privacy or metadata mismatch on iOS; everything else is parked. Post-3-0-backlog items that need no iPhone stay authorized (2026-10-16): each is closed in the change that fixes it, so it never takes an in-flight slot. The engine-remediation-2026-10 programme's unfinished items stay parked until the submission, then resume, except those the core overhaul takes up (decisions of 2026-11-10, below). Mac-only requests follow as items of this plan without changing the iPhone candidate. The CLI's shared History and its parity record and extended qualification (RF-30, RF-31) wait for the submission; the CLI 3.0 reads History but does not write it. The iPhone is used only in windows the maintainer announces. Nobody listens for 3.0: machine screens catch gross failures only, and the processed candidate gets risk-based acceptance. Restated on 2026-10-28 to match the decisions recorded since in RF-35 to RF-39; every earlier step, including superseded in-flight caps and the plan to archive the iPhone app from v3.0.0 itself, is in git log -p config/roadmap.json. Maintainer decisions of 2026-11-10: the target dates are removed from the roadmap and the release, so no item carries a due date and the order of work is set by gates; and the core overhaul of the runtime (the speed and memory work researched that day) is performed before the iOS App Store submission, which must be fully App Store compliant. The overhaul's items are RF-44 to RF-48: stages 0, 1, 2a, 3 and 4 of docs/audits/2026-11-10-apple-silicon-performance-research.md, the stages whose output is bit-identical. Its sample-changing stages are not in the plan. Maintainer decision of 2026-11-11: output quality is remediated before the iOS App Store submission. The findings verified in docs/audits/2026-11-11-qwen3-tts-quality-report-review.md become items RF-50 to RF-56 of this plan, taking up the matching parts of ER-03, ER-04, ER-05 and PA-16; the submission waits until the engine and its output are as good as they can be. The tooling, test procedures, benchmark harness and audio QC analysis the remediation leans on are audited too (RF-57). Nobody listens still: a change that alters samples lands only behind a machine screen whose decision rule is recorded before its takes are generated. Publishing a model artifact and moving a dependency pin still need the maintainer's specific request.

items.title: iPhone model downloads may use cellular data, off by default with an opt-in switch
items.gate: Maintainer decision 2026-10-24: Wi-Fi only stays the default, and a Download over cellular switch in Settings > Models & Files > Voice Models lets a download start over cellular. The background session allows cellular and each request carries the switch's value, so with it off nothing changes (Wi-Fi Assist cannot reroute a download); macOS is unchanged. Turning the switch on or off applies to downloads that start afterwards. Done when deterministic tests cover the request flag, the copy is in all ten interface languages, the control audit exercises the switch, the routed check passes, the Swift review finds no blocker, and, proportionate to the change (maintainer 2026-10-24), the new candidate passes the RF-15 navigation row and one model reinstall over Wi-Fi unattended, plus one attended check on cellular with Wi-Fi off: with the switch off a download waits, and with it on a download completes. The iPhone freeze moves to the commit that carries it.
items.notes: Opened 2026-10-24 after the freeze at e7a8e2ae, at the maintainer's request: Wi-Fi only (IOS-08, PA-21) kept people without Wi-Fi from installing any model; Wi-Fi Assist had rerouted flaky-Wi-Fi transfers over LTE, so per-request permission keeps that protection while the switch is off. Build 25, 2026-10-25: navigation row PASS (ios-xcui-candidate-smoke-20261025-030310-db58b35b) and the unattended Wi-Fi reinstall PASS (184700-55cd4a7d, switch off). Attended, 2026-10-27 on build 26 (maintainer): on 5G with no Wi-Fi and the switch off, a Voice Design download waits. It shows 682.3 MB (33%) from the start because speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors (682,293,092 bytes, the same SHA-256 in every model) is reused from the shared component store when an installed model holds it; reuse counts as progress with no network transfer. That matches the 682 MB seen on 2026-10-25, so those bytes were not cellular. The display is parked as BKL-39. With the switch on, a download started afterwards progressed over cellular (maintainer, 2026-10-27), then was stopped before it finished because coverage there is weak; a completion over cellular is not yet observed.

Each change keeps the fixed-seed PCM digest and shows a measured gain, no higher memory peak than the bands allow and no new interface hitches, on the Mac and, in an announced window, on the iPhone (report cards A1, A2, A4, A5).

items.notes: Opened 2026-11-10 with the overhaul; draws on ER-08's PERF-2 to PERF-6.
